The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the **RMS Titanic**.

To explain the complex concepts of blockchain technology using analogies, let's look at the provided description:

**1. The Digital Ledger as a Shared Notebook**
Imagine a traditional notebook used to record transactions. In a normal system, this notebook is kept in a single safe at a bank. If the bank is hacked or the notebook is lost, the records are compromised. In blockchain, imagine instead that every person in a large town has an identical copy of this notebook. This is the "decentralized" aspect. No single person holds the only copy; the information is distributed across many computers (the townspeople).

**2. Immutability and Verification as a Group Consensus**
Suppose you want to write a new entry in your notebook, such as "Alice paid Bob $10." In the blockchain system, you can't just write it down and keep it secret. You shout the transaction to the group. Everyone checks their own notebook to see if Alice actually has $10. If the majority agrees the transaction is valid, everyone writes the same new entry in their own notebooks at the same time.

**3. Security Through Redundancy**
Because everyone has a copy, if one person tries to cheat by changing their notebook to say "Alice paid Bob $1,000,000," the rest of the group will look at their own notebooks, see that the change doesn't match the majority, and reject it. The cheat’s notebook becomes an outlier and is ignored. This makes the system "extremely secure and trustworthy" because it is nearly impossible for a single point of failure or a malicious actor to alter the history without controlling more than half of all the copies, which is computationally very difficult.
